latin: Demones et animae peccatrices patiuntur ab igne, in quantum calidus est, afflictione eiusdem rationis cum ea qua affliguntur corpora.
translation: Demons and sinful souls suffer from fire, insofar as it is hot, with an affliction of the same kind as that by which bodies are afflicted.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch7, from Latin at farmer1998:12495

sources.text: Henry of Ghent, Quodlibet VIII, question 34
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit's identified source, discussing whether corporeal fire can afflict a spirit

doctrine: Farmer's note attaches the thesis to Peter Lombard's Sentences, book 4, distinction 44, questions 6-7, and suggests that Pico's interest lay in the metaphysical correspondence between physical and spiritual operations (paraphrase, farmer1998:12530). Edelheit reports that the question is discussed at Henry's Quodlibet VIII, question 34, where Henry takes up whether corporeal fire can cause affliction in a spirit, drawing on John of Damascus's view that only God is unlimited by anything, while an angel is limited by time and place (paraphrase, edelheit2022:15482, edelheit2022:15508).
historiography: Edelheit's chapter is the only scholarship on this thesis found in the material consulted; he quotes the thesis's Latin verbatim from the printed 900 Theses, page 242 (edelheit2022:15508).

quotations.text: It states that demons and sinful souls suffer from fire, inasmuch as it is hot, by a suffering of the same kind as that which bodies suffer.

not_established: Reception of this thesis beyond Edelheit's chapter, or any discussion of it in Pico's Apologia: not established by the sources consulted.
